Greetings of Christian love to one and all. In this issue of the magazine (Summer 2023)… The Church History article focuses on Bible prophecy pertaining to the end times and some various ways that over the years certain elements of the church got off track from the Biblical teaching as it pertained to their everyday life. In his article, Donny Brechbill, who together with his wife teaches multiple marriage seminars each year, endeavors to zone in on a challenging subject—some of the root problems that they see with women who are struggling in the church. Lee Rufener takes an unapologetic approach in his effort to share some expository teaching on practical ways to have a sanctified home. We have a new writer for the sisters this time who shares a burden on her heart—instilling God’s Word in the hearts of the next generation.

Plus, more interesting topics. Enjoy.

If you are edified or encouraged by any of the authors’ content, it would be a blessing for you to respond to us by mail or email. We pass this along to our writers for their benefit.

Recently, I was pondering the subject of change. As I have written before, we have gone through a fair bit of change as a family. During the last 1 to 2 years, we moved to another place of residence, I acquired a new job, and finally, praise the Lord, I have mostly recovered from most of the long-term effects of Covid. A special thanks to each one who has prayed for my health.

As I paused in quiet reminiscence, I was surprised by all the things that have changed in the 40-plus years that I can recall from memory. (Even though I am over 50 I really don’t remember much from the earliest years of my life.)

As a boy, I rode around in vehicles that had no seat belts and for sure, no airbags. When both of those “lifesaving” devices were first being introduced I well remember the many discussions whether they were truly lifesaving in their effect or whether the opposite was true. All vehicles used to be rear-wheel drive or four-wheel drive. How odd it seemed when the first front-wheel drive cars started to appear. Now we have hybrid vehicles with a push towards fully electric vehicles.

Forty-plus years ago, most farmers had gas-powered tractors with a carburetor or a diesel tractor with a manually powered injector pump. Today, most tractors are equipped with a computer and seemingly miles of wires and electronic this and electronic that. Back then, most farmers were able to maintain or repair their own equipment; now there is a need for diagnostic machines and specialized tools which cost a lot of money and take many hours to learn how to operate. This causes most farmers to rely on the expertise of specialized repairmen which also cost a lot of money.

Then there was Covid. That was a stressful time. Have you noticed what has changed during, after, or as a result of Covid? As I interact with others, routinely someone will say that this or that is different since Covid. Is it just me, or since Covid is the general public less friendly and more private with their interactions? Let’s check our own interactions to ensure that we are still being God’s “light” and “salt” to this dark world, and that we are not losing our “saltiness”. Also, there are help wanted signs everywhere. Why? It seems to me that Covid has encouraged what little work ethic was still flourishing in our society to diminish even further.

Then there is the issue of cell phones and E-bikes. What do these two disconnected products have in common? From my vantage point observing the Amish of Holmes County, these two items have done more to change a people and a culture in a more major way than almost anything else has in recent times.

Where does this all leave us? The Hebrew writer says that For the priesthood being changed, there is made of necessity a change also of the law –Hebrews 7:12. So, we see that God changed things as He saw fit, thus, if we need to change to become more Biblical, then we should. But the Apostle Paul says That we [should] henceforth be no more children, tossed to and fro, and carried about with every wind of doctrine… –Ephesians 4:14.

And because iniquity shall abound, the love of many shall wax cold. But he that shall endure unto the end, the same shall be saved –Matthew 24:12-13. So, let us be vigilant in these end times as change happens more and more around us. May we be among those who shall endure until the end.

以基督的爱向众人问安。在本期杂志（2023年夏季）……教会历史这一篇聚焦于有关末世的圣经预言，以及多年来教会在与日常生活相关的教导上某些方面如何偏离圣经教导的不同方式。在他的文章中，多尼·布雷奇比尔（Donny Brechbill）与妻子每年合办多场婚姻研讨会，努力把焦点放在一个具有挑战性的主题上——他们所见到的在教会中挣扎的妇女的一些根本问题。李·鲁费纳（Lee Rufener）以不妥协的态度，尽力分享关于怎样建立一个成圣家庭的实用阐释式教导。这次我们为姐妹们有一位新作者，她心中怀着一份负担——把神的话扎根在下一代的心里。

此外，还有更多有趣的主题。祝阅读愉快。

如果你从任一作者的内容中得着造就或鼓励，寄信或发电子邮件给我们会是极大的祝福。我们会把你的回馈转达给作者，供他们受益。

最近，我思考了变化这一课题。正如我以前写过的，作为一个家庭我们经历了相当多的变化。在过去一到两年间，我们搬了新居，我换了新工作，感谢主，我大部分从新冠的长期影响中恢复了。特别感谢为我的健康祷告的每一位。

当我在静默中回想时，我对在我记忆中可回溯的四十多年里发生的所有变化感到惊讶。（尽管我已过五十，幼年最早的岁月我确实记得不多。）

小时候，我坐过的车没有安全带，更别说安全气囊了。当这两种“救命”装置刚被引入时，我还清楚地记得许多关于它们是否真能救命或是否反而有害的讨论。所有车过去通常都是后轮驱动或四轮驱动。当第一批前轮驱动车出现时觉得多么奇怪。现在我们有了混合动力车，并正推动向纯电动车过渡。

四十多年前，大多数农民使用的是带化油器的汽油拖拉机或带手动喷油泵的柴油拖拉机。如今，大多数拖拉机都装有电脑以及看似延绵不绝的电线和各种电子装置。那时大多数农民能够自己维护或修理设备；现在需要诊断机器和专用工具，这些都很昂贵且需要许多小时学习操作。这导致大多数农民依赖专业维修人员的专门技能，而这也很花钱。

然后是新冠疫情。那是一段充满压力的时期。你有没有注意到在疫情期间、之后或由疫情引起的变化？当我与他人交往时，常有人说自从新冠后这或那变得不同了。是只有我觉得如此，还是自从新冠以来公众在交往上变得更不友好、更注重私人空间？让我们检查自己的交往，确保我们仍是这黑暗世界中的神的“光”和“盐”，并且不失去我们的“咸味”。此外，到处都挂着招工启事。为什么？在我看来，新冠促使社会中那本已不多的职业道德进一步衰退。

还有手机和电动自行车的问题。这两种看似无关的产品有什么共同点？从我观察霍姆斯县阿米什人的视角来看，这两样东西比近来几乎任何其他事物都更大程度地改变了一个民族和一种文化。

这一切把我们带到哪里？希伯来书的作者说：祭司职任既然改变，律法也必有改变。——希伯来书 7:12。因此，我们看到神随自己的旨意改变事物，所以，若我们需要改变以更合乎圣经，我们就应当如此。但使徒保罗说：叫我们不再作小孩子，随波逐流，被各样的风俗所吹动。——以弗所书 4:14。

罪恶增多，许人的爱心才冷淡了；唯有忍耐到底的，必然得救。——马太福音 24:12-13。所以，当周围的变化愈来愈多时，让我们在这些末日里保持警醒。愿我们成为那些能忍耐到底的人之一。

“My, it’s warm!” exclaimed Mom. “A nice, good rain is what we need to cool things off a bit.”

It was Saturday, near the end of June, and the weather had been particularly hot and humid that day. Ellie’s mother had been cleaning the house and preparing some food for the company that was invited to come for lunch on Sunday after church.

As the afternoon moved into early evening, it felt like it became even hotter, and no breezes were to be found. Ellie’s father was resting in a hammock out on the lawn while the rest of the family tried to find the most comfortable place to seek relief from the heat.

As evening approached, so did the clouds. They arrived suddenly, along with gusts of wind that began to stir up the dust. Lightning started to flash across the sky and the thunder rumbled in the distance.

“Quickly, children!” called Mom. “Put away your toys; it’s about to storm!”

Ellie looked around in alarm. It was getting dark very quickly and the sky looked strange—almost angry. She quickly gathered up her playthings and hurried into the house. Dad was no longer sleeping on the hammock. The wind had almost toppled it over and him along with it! He, too, hurried into the house; the wind causing the door to slam violently behind him. The family gathered on the sunporch to watch the approaching storm. There were windows to the west and south, so they had a good vantage point from which to watch the coming rain. The wind was blowing with a force that Ellie had never experienced in all her seven years. She noted the concern and alarm on her parents’ faces as they watched and waited.

Then it began to rain. Great sheets of rain were being driven against the windows and Ellie wondered if it was possible that it was raining hard enough to break the glass.

“What was that?” exclaimed Mom as suddenly, a sheet of tin whizzed past the sunporch windows and disappeared beyond the garden.

“I think it’s part of the garage roof,” said Dad in disbelief while peering cautiously through the windows.

Upon hearing this, Mom directed the children to stand by the cellar door. If things got worse, down they would go! Ellie felt so scared. What was going to happen to them? Would their house blow away? Would any of them get hurt?

As abruptly as the storm began, it calmed. The wind stopped, the rain slowed, and very soon the sun was shining again. The family cautiously ventured outdoors to see what all had happened during the storm.

“Look!” said Dad. “The garage roof is gone and so is the south wall!”

“Why does Gerald’s house look so strange?” Mom pointed toward their next-door neighbors. “Why, look! The entire roof is gone from their house!” Indeed, the roof had been cleanly stripped away and the gable ends stoically stood there, holding up nothing.

The wail of sirens could be heard in the distance and as they looked around the neighborhood, they could see smoke just beyond some trees.

“That’s got to be Melvin’s barn burning!” exclaimed Dad. “I’m going to go see what I can do to help.” He raced for his truck and was soon hurrying out the driveway.

The winds had been so strong that some electric poles were blown over causing the electricity to be disconnected so there were no lights or fans. After the storm had passed the humidity and heat had returned making the night hot and muggy. Yet the grown-ups from the area worked long into the night, helping each other to clean up what they could of the storm damage.

Of special interest was our neighbor Melvin. His barn had collapsed on top of dozens of cattle and then a fire had broken out. The neighbor men tried desperately to rescue what cattle they could, but in the end, many of the steers could not be saved.

Sunday came, but no one went to church. The morning was spent over at Melvin’s, hauling away dead cattle, clearing away burnt hay, and simply just being there for one another. It was hard, grim work. Ellie clearly remembers how awful the smell was. And she could barely bring herself to watch the loading up of the dead steers. When lunch time came, their company arrived, but no one was very hungry. Ellie’s younger brother sobbed, “All I can think about is those poor steers!”

Ellie was surprised how powerful a storm could be. And scary! Would they experience another twister? Might more buildings collapse, and another barn or house burn down? A seed of fear began to grow in Ellie’s heart. Throughout that summer and for many summers after, every time the rumble of thunder was heard or she heard the words “tornado warning”, her heart would beat faster, and a knot would settle in her stomach. How she dreaded each storm! She wished they would all just pass by their home. Why did God allow storms, anyway?

“You need to trust God, Ellie,” her mother would say. “He’s the One who made the weather, and He is in control of everything that happens. He might not always keep us from experiencing frightening times, but He is always there to take care of us.”

As she grew older, Ellie learned to take this advice to heart. Her fear of storms faded, and, in its place, she developed a fascination with how storms develop and form. Knowing that God is the Master of the wind is still a comfort and an assurance to her. Most of all, as she has learned to trust God in every area of her life, she has found Him to always be faithful. Learning to replace fear with trust always brings peace to the heart.

“Ag, dis warm!” roep Ma uit. “’n Goeie, ligte reën is wat ons nodig het om dit ’n bietjie af te koel.”

Dit was Saterdag, teen die einde van Junie, en die weer was daardie dag besonder warm en vogtig. Ellie se ma was besig om die huis skoon te maak en om kos voor te berei vir die gaste wat vir Sondagmiddag na die kerk uitgenooi was.

Terwyl die middag in die vroeë aand oorgaan het, het dit gevoel asof dit nog warmer raak, en daar was geen briesies om te vind nie. Ellie se pa het in ’n hangmat op die grasperk gerus terwyl die res van die gesin probeer het om die gemaklikste plek te vind om verligting van die hitte te kry.

Soos die aand nader gekom het, het die wolke ook nader gekom. Hulle het skielik opgedaag, saam met windstote wat die stof begin opskerp het. Blits het oor die hemel gespat en die donder het in die verte gerommel.

“Klaar vinnig, kinders!” het Ma geroep. “Berg julle speelgoed weg; dit gaan storm!”

Ellie het met alarm rondgekyk. Dit het baie vinnig donker geword en die hemel het snaaks gelyk—byna kwaad. Sy het gou haar speelding bymekaar gemaak en huis toe gehaas. Pa het nie meer in die hangmat geslaap nie. Die wind het dit amper omgeslaan en hom saam daarmee! Hy het ook vinnig huis toe gehaas; die wind het die deur hard agter hom toegeslaan. Die gesin het op die sonstoep bymekaargekom om die naderende storm te beskou. Daar was vensters na die weste en suide, so hulle het ’n goeie uitkykpunt gehad om die komende reën te kyk. Die wind het met ’n krag gewaai wat Ellie nog nooit in haar sewe jaar ervaar het nie. Sy het die kommer en vrees op haar ouers se gesigte opgemerk terwyl hulle gekyk en gewag het.

Toe het dit begin reën. Groot matjies reën is teen die vensters gedryf en Ellie het gewonder of dit moontlik was dat dit so hard reën dat die glas kon bars.

“Wat was dit?” het Ma uitgerys toe skielik ’n sinkvel verby die sonstoepvensters flits en buite die tuin verdwyn het.

“Ek dink dit is ’n deel van die motorhuisdak,” het Pa ongelowig gesê terwyl hy versigtig deur die vensters loer.

By die hoor hiervan het Ma die kinders beveel om by die kelderdeur te staan. As dinge erger word, sal hulle daaronder ingaan! Ellie het so bang gevoel. Wat gaan met hulle gebeur? Sal hul huis wegwaai? Sal iemand van hulle beseer word?

Net so skielik soos die storm begin het, het dit bedaar. Die wind het opgehou, die reën het stadig geword, en baie gou het die son weer geskyn. Die gesin het versigtig buite uitgegaan om te sien wat tydens die storm gebeur het.

“Kyk!” het Pa gesê. “Die motorhuisdak is weg en so ook die suidmuur!”

“Hoekom lyk Gerald se huis so vreemd?” het Ma na hul buurman verwys. “Kyk tog! Die hele dak is van hul huis af weggeskeur!” Inderdaad, die dak was netjies weggesny en die sypunte het stoïes daar gestaan en niks gedra nie.

Die sirenes se huil kon in die verte gehoor word en toe hulle in die buurt rondkyk, kon hulle rook net agter ’n paar bome sien.

“Dit moet Melvin se skuur wees wat brand!” het Pa uitgeroep. “Ek gaan sien wat ek kan doen om te help.” Hy het sy vragmotor gegryp en gou die opritte uitgejaag.

Die winde was so sterk dat sommige kragposte omgewaai het, wat veroorsaak het dat die elektriese krag afgesny is, so daar was geen ligte of waaiers nie. Nadat die storm verby was, het die humiditeit en hitte teruggekeer en die nag warm en drukkend gemaak. Tog het die grootmense van die area lank in die nag gewerk en mekaar gehelp om op te ruim wat hulle van die stormskade kon.

Van besondere belang was ons buurman Melvin. Sy skuur het op dosyne beeste ingestort en toe het ’n vuur uitgebreek. Die manlike bure het desperaat probeer om so baie beeste as moontlik te red, maar uiteindelik kon baie van die bulte nie gespaar word nie.

Sondag het gekom, maar niemand het kerk toe gegaan nie. Die oggend is by Melvin deurgebring, doodbeeste uitruilend, verbrand hooi wegruimend, en net daar wees vir mekaar. Dit was harde, grim werksaamheid. Ellie onthou duidelik hoe afgryslik die reuk was. En sy kon skaars na die laai van die dooie bulte kyk. Toe dit tyd vir middagete was, het hul gaste aangekom, maar niemand was regtig honger nie. Ellie se jonger broer het gehuil: “Alles waaraan ek kan dink is daardie armes bulle!”

Ellie was verras hoe kragtig ’n storm kon wees. En eng! Sou hulle ’n ander tornado ervaar? Sou meer geboue kan instort, en sou nog ’n skuur of huis afbrand? ’n Saadjie van vrees het in Ellie se hart begin groei. Gedurende daardie somer en vir baie somers daarna, elke keer as die donder gerommel is of sy die woorde “tornado waarskuwing” gehoor het, het haar hart vinniger geklop en ’n knoop het in haar maag kom sit. Hoe sy elke storm gegroet het! Sy het gewens hulle sou net almal verby hul huis gaan. Waarom het God storms toegelaat, eintlik?

“Jy moet God vertrou, Ellie,” het haar moeder gesê. “Hy is Degene wat die weer gemaak het, en Hy het beheer oor alles wat gebeur. Hy sal ons dalk nie altyd teen vreeslike tye bewaar nie, maar Hy is altyd daar om na ons om te sien.”

Toe sy ouer geword het, het Ellie geleer om hierdie raad ter harte te neem. Haar vrees vir storms het vervaag, en in die plek daarvan het sy ’n belangstelling ontwikkel in hoe storms ontwikkel en vorm. Om te weet dat God die Meester van die wind is, is steeds ’n troos en ’n sekerheid vir haar. Mees van alles, soos sy geleer het om God in elke area van haar lewe te vertrou, het sy Hom altyd getrou gevind. Om vrees met vertroue te vervang bring altyd vrede in die hart.

I watched as a man attempted to cut a large sheet of plywood in half. He was talking with a few other men while he was cutting, and it seemed that he wasn’t too concerned about making the cut straight. I noticed that he continued to cut further and further from the line that he had scratched into the piece of plywood with a nail. After he was several inches off, one of his friends tried to point it out but he pretended to ignore him. He tried to casually guide the old handsaw back towards the line, while continuing to talk with the men, not making a big deal of it. Finally, after he was more than a foot off, he stopped. He knew now that he had a problem, a problem he could not fix.

I had to think, “Is this what we are doing as the church, the bride of Christ?” We are not too serious about drifting off the straight and narrow way; we allow things to come into our midst. We say, “It’s not a big deal, let’s not be critical.” But the longer we wait, the harder it will be to straighten out. At first it shocks us; later it becomes the new normal. How do we tell if we have drifted? It should be as easy as considering where we used to be, and comparing it that with where we are now, then evaluating the change with what the Bible teaches.

Since fighting against drift is not popular, men in the church don’t want to do it. Some people in our churches who are drifting towards the world have perfected a feel-good gospel. They go on and on about how close they are getting to Jesus, and how blessed they are, but their direction is clearly not in line with the teachings of Scripture. They’re headed towards the world.

There are others who don’t want the church to drift, yet they have their own problems—the love of money, covetousness, and a love of pleasure. No one says anything because it seems that nobody wants to hear. A popular response is, “Yes, I know it’s not good, but what can we do?” “All churches have problems.” Or “Yes, I would never allow that, but I don’t feel it’s in my place to speak up about it.” “It’s not for my family, but if others want to do that, its fine.”

We live in a “me” age. Everything is about me. The conservative, Anabaptist people are getting tangled up in social media, selfies, tweeting, Facebook, and you name it. We love ourselves to the extent that we talk, act, and dress in ways that draw attention to ourselves—we promote ourselves. We talk about looking good, feeling good, and living good. What happened to promoting Jesus? Remember, Jesus said: For whosoever will save his life shall lose it: and whosoever will lose his life for my sake shall find it –Matthew 16:25.

Why does it seem so hard to tell which direction we are going? If we are all about ourselves, then we are not all about Jesus. If we are into the latest fashions and the nicest cars, trucks, and houses, then we are not all about Jesus. We cannot indulge ourselves in pleasing the flesh, and still say we are Christians.

I was recently asked why some pastors lose their children to the world. In most cases, I believe it’s the same reason that many Anabaptists are losing their children to the kingdom of darkness—the fathers have lost a godly vision for their homes. They live a powerless life and allow the world to come in. Maybe they do not have television, but what about the internet? This still allows the influence of the world to come in. Also, Dad spends more time with his business and more time enjoying life than he does seeking the face of God.

Many Americans go on short-term missions. Many times, it seems that the youth who go want to hit the beach or some other pleasure and relaxation as soon as they get off the plane. Why? Because that’s what they are either taught or allowed to do back home—seek pleasure. They haven’t been taught to deny the flesh; they haven’t seen their parents deny the flesh. Some of us might be so far off the mark that we need to do like the carpenter at the beginning of this article—Humble ourselves and start over.

Husbands are pulling their unwilling wives into the world, wives are pushing their husbands into the world, and children are dragging their parents into the world. And unfortunately, since the modern church has thrown off all forms of discipline and structure, everyone can stay in the church and pollute it with their worldly ideas (at least as long as you smile and say you love Jesus.) Remember the Scriptures: If ye love me, keep my commandments –John 14:15. And, He that saith, I know him, and keepeth not his commandments, is a liar, and the truth is not in him –1 John 2:4.

Here are some areas of drift in the church.

Brotherly love

By this shall all men know that ye are my disciples, if ye have love one to another –John 13:35.

People have visited our church and asked if we practice the holy kiss. I reply that we do; however, understanding the need to love one another comes first. Many churches are doing away with the holy kiss, which is clearly instructed in the Word. And it seems appropriate because they have stopped loving one another. I don’t believe we understand the importance of this topic—having love one for another. When our love causes us to suffer for one another, the world sees it. Often, the reason a brotherhood stops loving each other is because they are not in the fight “together” anymore. They have become independent.

Some of the greatest acts of showing love for one another have happened on the battlefield. Men have jumped on grenades, and they have jumped in front of bullets to save their comrades. Because they have fought together, they look out for each other. What if a soldier marching out to battle would notice a fellow soldier’s ammunition clip fall from his gun? What would he do? Would he remain quiet because his comrade might get mad? Or would he remain quiet because he knew that he had his own problems? No. He would help his brother. If ungodly men on the battlefield can practice this, why can’t God’s people do so in the church? Before I was converted, I was in the military. I chose to suffer for my country. Now that I’m a Christian, I now choose to suffer for my Lord.

Dress

This is the most obvious, but also the most overlooked. The worldly church says, “It’s the heart that counts, so how we appear on the outside doesn’t matter”. Are the Anabaptists falling for this? The world used to dress modestly, but television and Hollywood began to promote a focus on the human body. Surely the church wouldn’t follow Hollywood. But what is the difference—a woman of the world who is obviously dressed immodestly, or a woman of the church dressed with a cape dress that is form-fitting, and with a little covering hanging skimpily on the back of her head? There is little difference, except the one claims to be a Christian and the other one doesn’t. Dear ones, the world is laughing at us.

So how does it all start? Subtly. First remove a pleat here or a gather there, then start using a little less material, finally, start buying brighter bolder colors. The men untuck the shirt, switch to jeans, then skinny jeans, undo a few buttons, grow out the hair a little. Buy a pair of the “cool” name brand shoes, and a cowboy hat. The devil is no fool. If you drop a frog into boiling water, it will jump out quickly. If you boil the water that contains the frog, he will slowly cook to death. Is it too late for us to jump out? With God all things are possible. Brothers and sisters, it is the heart that counts; and if we desire to look like the world, our heart is worldly and needs to be cleaned—cleaned by the ever so powerful blood of Jesus.

Pleasure

Ye have lived in pleasure on the earth, and been wanton; ye have nourished your hearts, as in a day of slaughter. Ye have condemned and killed the just; and he doth not resist you –James 5:5-6.

And that which fell among thorns are they, which, when they have heard, go forth, and are choked with cares and riches and pleasures of this life, and bring no fruit to perfection –Luke 8:14.

This know also, that in the last days perilous times shall come. For men shall be lovers of their own selves, covetous, boasters, proud, blasphemers, disobedient to parents, unthankful, unholy, Without natural affection, trucebreakers, false accusers, incontinent, fierce, despisers of those that are good, Traitors, heady, highminded, lovers of pleasures more than lovers of God; Having a form of godliness, but denying the power thereof: from such turn away –2 Timothy 3:1-5.

When we are given to pleasure, we separate ourselves from the sufferings we have been called to, therefore separating us from the reward received from suffering.

Remember, when we give in a little on any issue during our generation, our children will go farther with it. When our children enjoy going to church only because of the volleyball game that’s scheduled afterward, it’s not good. When they want to go on a mission trip because of the pleasures of the ocean, it’s not good. I’m not saying those things are bad, but when they become the focal point, we have a serious problem. Do we enjoy doing the things that God enjoys? Do we enjoy hymn sings anymore? Do we enjoy helping the poor? What about visiting the widows? I believe if the fathers have their priorities right, and they truly love doing the things of God even if the flesh suffers, then so will our children, (the next generation) for which WE are responsible. I often tell people that they don’t need to follow Jesus. They can love the world, and the pleasures of this life, but they cannot continue sitting in our church and pretend they are Christians. People might say that’s too harsh, but I believe Jesus said the same thing. I know thy works, that thou art neither cold nor hot: I would thou wert cold or hot. So then because thou art lukewarm, and neither cold nor hot, I will spue thee out of my mouth –Revelation 3:15-16.

This is not a complete list as there are many other ways that the church is drifting towards the world. My prayer is that, first, we could see the problem, and second, we could deal with it. Remember a little leaven leavens the lump. (1 Corinthians 5)

There is a battle that’s raging; the kingdom of darkness is pressing in. The devil truly knows he has but a short time. Let us make a stand, put down our white flags, and pick up our swords. Let us remove the traitors, the world, and the sin that has come into the church. Let us purify the church and fight the good fight of faith.

How do we stop the drift? How do we leave behind a faithful generation? First, the fathers need to teach their children, and the leaders in the church need to teach them all. The early Anabaptists met as many times as they could, and that was usually out in the weather, in some woods somewhere. Our church here meets five times a week. Meeting on Sundays only, I believe, shows where our priorities are.

And he gave some, apostles; and some, prophets; and some, evangelists; and some, pastors and teachers; For the perfecting of the saints, for the work of the ministry, for the edifying of the body of Christ: Till we all come in the unity of the faith, and of the knowledge of the Son of God, unto a perfect man, unto the measure of the stature of the fulness of Christ: – Ephesians 4:11-13.

It seems that God would give us teachers, pastors, evangelists, prophets, and apostles if we would use them.

Let’s make this personal—there could be areas of drift in my life. We need to help each other before we all drift into ruin. Maybe we can maintain, but we also need to be concerned about our children. If we could get together and be honest with ourselves and with one another about what the scriptures clearly teach, then we would be more careful. If we could study God’s Word together, with open hearts and minds, I believe we could strengthen that which remains. I believe if we would fall on our faces before God, He would heal our churches. May God bless us all in a deeper walk with Him.

Aku melihat seorang laki-laki mencoba memotong selembar papan lapis besar menjadi dua. Dia sedang bercakap dengan beberapa lelaki lain sementara memotong, dan tampak bahwa dia tidak terlalu khawatir mengenai membuat potongan yang lurus. Aku memperhatikan bahwa dia terus memotong semakin jauh dari garis yang telah dia goreskan pada potongan papan lapis itu dengan paku. Setelah ia beberapa inci melenceng, salah seorang temannya mencoba menunjukkannya tetapi ia berpura-pura mengabaikannya. Ia coba dengan santai mengarahkan gergaji tangan tua itu kembali ke garis, sambil terus bercakap dengan mereka, seolah-olah tidak ada masalah besar. Akhirnya, setelah ia lebih dari satu kaki melenceng, ia berhenti. Sekarang ia tahu bahwa ia punya masalah, masalah yang tidak dapat ia perbaiki.

Aku harus berpikir, "Apakah inikah yang kita lakukan sebagai jemaat, mempelai perempuan Kristus?" Kita tidak terlalu serius mengenai melenceng dari jalan yang lurus dan sempit; kita membiarkan hal-hal masuk ke tengah-tengah kita. Kita berkata, "Ini bukan masalah besar, jangan kritis." Tetapi semakin lama kita menunggu, semakin sulit untuk meluruskan kembali. Pada awalnya itu mengejutkan kita; kemudian itu menjadi kebiasaan baru. Bagaimana kita tahu apakah kita telah melenceng? Sepatutnya semudah mempertimbangkan di mana kita dulu berada, membandingkannya dengan di mana kita sekarang berada, lalu mengevaluasi perubahan itu dengan apa yang diajarkan Alkitab.

Karena melawan arus tidak populer, orang-orang di gereja tidak mau melakukannya. Beberapa orang di gereja kita yang sedang melenceng menuju dunia telah menyempurnakan injil yang membuat merasa enak. Mereka terus-menerus membicarakan betapa dekatnya mereka kepada Yesus, dan betapa diberkatinya mereka, tetapi arah mereka jelas tidak selaras dengan ajaran Kitab Suci. Mereka sedang menuju kepada dunia.

Ada pula mereka yang tidak mau gereja melenceng, namun mereka punya masalah sendiri—cinta akan uang, kerakusan, dan cinta akan kesenangan. Tak seorangpun berkata apa-apa karena tampaknya tidak ada yang mau mendengarkan. Respon yang populer adalah, "Ya, aku tahu itu tidak baik, tetapi apa yang bisa kita lakukan?" "Semua gereja punya masalah." Atau "Ya, aku tidak akan pernah mengizinkan itu, tetapi aku tidak merasa tempatku untuk berbicara soal itu." "Bukan untuk keluargaku, tetapi jika orang lain ingin melakukan itu, tidak apa-apa."

Kita hidup di zaman "aku". Segalanya tentang aku. Orang-orang Anabaptis yang konservatif tersangkut dalam media sosial, selfie, tweeting, Facebook, dan segala macamnya. Kita sangat mencintai diri sendiri sampai kita berbicara, bertindak, dan berpakaian dengan cara yang menarik perhatian kita sendiri—kita mempromosikan diri kita sendiri. Kita berbicara tentang tampak baik, merasa baik, dan hidup baik. Ke mana perginya mempromosikan Yesus? Ingat, Yesus berkata: Sebab barangsiapa mau menyelamatkan nyawanya, ia akan kehilangan itu; tetapi barangsiapa kehilangan nyawanya karena Aku, ia akan memperolehnya –Matthew 16:25.

Mengapa tampaknya begitu sulit mengetahui arah yang kita tuju? Jika kita semuanya tentang diri sendiri, maka kita bukan semuanya tentang Yesus. Jika kita mengikuti mode terbaru dan kendaraan, rumah terbaik, maka kita tidak semuanya tentang Yesus. Kita tidak dapat memanjakan diri demi menyenangkan daging, lalu masih mengatakan kita orang Kristen.

Aku baru-baru ini ditanya mengapa beberapa pendeta kehilangan anak-anak mereka kepada dunia. Dalam banyak kasus, aku percaya itu karena alasan yang sama mengapa banyak orang Anabaptis kehilangan anak-anak mereka kepada kerajaan kegelapan—para ayah telah kehilangan visi yang saleh untuk rumah tangga mereka. Mereka hidup tanpa kuasa dan membiarkan dunia masuk. Mungkin mereka tidak punya televisi, tetapi bagaimana dengan internet? Ini tetap memungkinkan pengaruh dunia masuk. Juga, Ayah menghabiskan lebih banyak waktu untuk bisnisnya dan lebih banyak menikmati hidup daripada mencari wajah Allah.

Banyak orang Amerika pergi dalam pelayanan singkat. Seringkali tampak bahwa kaum muda yang pergi ingin langsung ke pantai atau mencari kesenangan dan relaksasi lainnya begitu turun dari pesawat. Mengapa? Karena itulah yang mereka diajarkan atau diizinkan untuk dilakukan di rumah—mencari kesenangan. Mereka belum diajarkan menyangkal daging; mereka belum melihat orang tua mereka menyangkal daging. Beberapa dari kita mungkin begitu jauh melenceng sehingga perlu melakukan seperti tukang kayu di awal artikel ini—merendahkan diri dan mulai kembali.

Suami menarik istri yang enggan ke dalam dunia, istri mendorong suami ke dalam dunia, dan anak-anak menyeret orang tua mereka ke dalam dunia. Dan sayangnya, karena gereja modern telah menanggalkan segala bentuk disiplin dan struktur, setiap orang bisa tetap dalam gereja dan mencemarinya dengan gagasan-gagasan duniawi mereka (setidaknya selama kamu tersenyum dan berkata kamu mengasihi Yesus). Ingat Kitab Suci: Jikalau kamu mengasihi Aku, kamu akan menuruti segala perintah-Ku –John 14:15. Dan barangsiapa berkata: Aku mengenal Dia, tetapi ia tidak menuruti perintah-Nya, ia adalah pendusta, dan kebenaran tidak ada di dalam dia –1 John 2:4.

Berikut beberapa bidang di mana gereja melenceng.

Kasih persaudaraan

Dari adanya kasih itu semua orang akan tahu, bahwa kamu adalah murid-murid-Ku: yaitu jikalau kamu saling mengasihi –John 13:35.

Orang-orang pernah mengunjungi gereja kami dan bertanya apakah kami mempraktikkan ciuman kudus. Aku menjawab bahwa kami melakukannya; namun, memahami kebutuhan untuk saling mengasihi harus didahulukan. Banyak gereja menghilangkan praktik ciuman kudus, yang jelas diperintahkan dalam Firman. Dan itu tampak tepat karena mereka telah berhenti saling mengasihi. Aku tidak percaya kita memahami pentingnya topik ini—memiliki kasih seorang kepada yang lain. Ketika kasih kita menyebabkan kita menderita demi satu sama lain, dunia melihatnya. Seringkali, alasan persaudaraan berhenti saling mengasihi adalah karena mereka tidak lagi berjuang "bersama". Mereka menjadi mandiri.

Beberapa tindakan terbesar untuk menunjukkan kasih kepada satu sama lain terjadi di medan perang. Orang-orang telah melompat menutupi ranjau, dan mereka telah melompat di depan peluru untuk menyelamatkan sahabat mereka. Karena mereka telah berjuang bersama, mereka saling menjaga. Bagaimana jika seorang prajurit yang berbaris ke medan perang melihat klip amunisi rekan prajuritnya terjatuh dari senjatanya? Apa yang akan dia lakukan? Akankah dia tetap diam karena rekannya mungkin marah? Atau akankah dia tetap diam karena dia tahu ia punya masalah sendiri? Tidak. Dia akan menolong saudaranya. Jika orang-orang yang tak takut Tuhan di medan perang dapat mempraktikkan ini, mengapa umat Allah tidak bisa melakukannya di dalam gereja? Sebelum aku bertobat, aku pernah di militer. Aku memilih menderita demi negaraku. Sekarang aku seorang Kristen, aku memilih menderita demi Tuhanku.

Pakaian

Ini yang paling jelas, tetapi juga yang paling diabaikan. Gereja duniawi berkata, "Yang penting adalah hati, jadi bagaimana kita tampak di luar tidak penting." Apakah orang-orang Anabaptis tertipu oleh ini? Dahulu dunia berpakaian sopan, tetapi televisi dan Hollywood mulai mempromosikan fokus pada tubuh manusia. Tentu saja gereja tidak akan mengikuti Hollywood. Tetapi apa bedanya—seorang perempuan duniawi yang jelas berpakaian tidak sopan, atau seorang perempuan gereja berpakaian dengan gaun mantel yang ketat, dan dengan penutup kecil tergantung tipis di belakang kepalanya? Hampir tidak ada bedanya, kecuali yang satu mengaku Kristen dan yang lain tidak. Saudara-saudara, dunia sedang menertawakan kita.

Lalu bagaimana semuanya dimulai? Secara halus. Pertama hilangkan satu lipatan di sini atau satu kumpulan kain di sana, lalu mulai gunakan sedikit bahan, akhirnya, mulai membeli warna yang lebih cerah dan lebih berani. Para pria masukkan baju keluar, beralih ke jins, lalu jeans skinny, membuka beberapa kancing, memanjangkan rambut sedikit. Beli sepasang sepatu merek "keren", dan topi koboi. Iblis bukan orang bodoh. Jika kamu menjatuhkan seekor katak ke dalam air yang mendidih, ia akan melompat keluar dengan cepat. Jika kamu merebus air yang berisi katak itu, ia akan perlahan-lahan mati direbus. Apakah sudah terlambat bagi kita untuk melompat keluar? Dengan Allah semua perkara mungkin. Saudara-saudara, hati yang penting; dan jika kita ingin tampak seperti dunia, hati kita duniawi dan perlu dibersihkan—dibersihkan oleh darah Yesus yang sangat kuat itu.

Kesenangan

Kamu hidup dalam kesenangan di bumi, dan bermewah-mewah; kamu telah menggemukkan hatimu untuk hari pembunuhan. Kamu telah menghakimi dan telah membunuh orang benar; dan ia tidak melawan kamu –James 5:5-6.

Dan yang ditaburkan di antara duri ialah mereka yang, setelah mereka mendengar, berjalan bersama-sama dan tercekik oleh kekhawatiran dan kekayaan dan kesenangan hidup ini dan tidak menghasilkan buah sampai sempurna –Luke 8:14.

Ketahuilah juga, pada hari-hari terakhir akan datang masa-masa sukar. Karena manusia akan menjadi pencinta diri sendiri, tamak, pemegah diri, sombong, menghujat, tidak taat kepada orang tua, tidak tahu berterima kasih, tidak suci, tanpa kasih alamiah, pemecah perjanjian, pencela, tak berahi, ganas, pembenci yang baik, pengkhianat, lekas marah, tinggi hati, pencinta kesenangan lebih dari pencinta Allah, mereka mempunyai rupa ibadah, tetapi menyangkal kuasa-Nya: dari mereka jauhilah –2 Timothy 3:1-5.

Ketika kita memberi diri kepada kesenangan, kita memisahkan diri dari penderitaan yang kita dipanggil untuk mengikutinya, sehingga memisahkan kita dari upah yang diterima karena penderitaan itu.

Ingat, ketika kita sedikit memberi kelonggaran pada suatu isu pada generasi kita, anak-anak kita akan melangkah lebih jauh dengannya. Ketika anak-anak kita senang pergi ke gereja hanya karena ada permainan voli yang dijadwalkan setelahnya, itu tidak baik. Ketika mereka ingin pergi dalam perjalanan misi karena kesenangan laut, itu tidak baik. Aku tidak mengatakan hal-hal itu buruk, tetapi ketika hal-hal itu menjadi titik fokus, kita punya masalah serius. Apakah kita menikmati melakukan hal-hal yang disukai Allah? Apakah kita masih menikmati menyanyi himne? Apakah kita menikmati menolong orang miskin? Bagaimana dengan mengunjungi janda-janda? Aku percaya jika para ayah menata prioritas mereka dengan benar, dan mereka benar-benar suka melakukan perkara-perkara Allah meskipun daging menderita, maka anak-anak kita juga demikian, (generasi berikutnya) yang menjadi TANGGUNG JAWAB KITA. Aku sering mengatakan kepada orang-orang bahwa mereka tidak perlu mengikuti Yesus. Mereka boleh mencintai dunia, dan kesenangan hidup ini, tetapi mereka tidak dapat terus duduk di gereja kita dan pura-pura bahwa mereka adalah orang Kristen. Orang mungkin berkata itu terlalu keras, tetapi aku percaya Yesus berkata hal yang sama. Aku tahu segala pekerjaanmu—engkau tidak dingin dan tidak panas: alangkah baiknya kalau engkau dingin atau panas. Karena engkau suam-suam kuku dan bukan dingin dan bukan panas, Aku akan memuntahkan engkau dari mulut-Ku –Revelation 3:15-16.

Ini bukan daftar lengkap karena masih banyak cara lain gereja melenceng menuju dunia. Doaku adalah, pertama, semoga kita dapat melihat masalah ini, dan kedua, semoga kita dapat menanganinya. Ingat sejumput ragi menggurihkan seluruh adonan. (1 Corinthians 5)

Ada pertempuran yang sedang berkecamuk; kerajaan kegelapan menekan masuk. Iblis sungguh tahu bahwa ia hanya mempunyai waktu singkat. Marilah kita berdiri tegak, turunkan bendera putih kita, dan angkat pedang kita. Marilah kita singkirkan para pengkhianat, dunia, dan dosa yang telah masuk ke dalam gereja. Marilah kita membersihkan gereja dan berjuang mempertahankan iman yang baik.

Bagaimana kita menghentikan penyimpangan? Bagaimana kita meninggalkan generasi yang setia? Pertama, para ayah perlu mengajar anak-anak mereka, dan para pemimpin di gereja perlu mengajar mereka semua. Orang-orang Anabaptis awal bertemu sebanyak mungkin waktu yang mereka bisa, dan itu biasanya di luar, di semak belukar mana pun. Gereja kami di sini berkumpul lima kali seminggu. Bertemu hanya pada hari Minggu, menurutku, menunjukkan di mana prioritas kita.

Dan Ia memberikan sebagian sebagai rasul-rasul, sebagian sebagai nabi-nabi, sebagian sebagai pemberita-pemberita injil, dan sebagian sebagai gembala-gembala dan pengajar-pengajar, untuk memperlengkapi orang-orang kudus bagi pekerjaan pelayanan, bagi pembangunan tubuh Kristus, sampai kita semua mencapai persatuan iman dan pengenalan tentang Anak Allah, menjadi manusia yang sempurna, sampai ukuran kepenuhan Kristus – Ephesians 4:11-13.

Tampaknya Allah akan memberi kita pengajar, gembala, pemberita Injil, nabi, dan rasul jika kita mau memakai mereka.

Mari kita jadikan ini pribadi—mungkin ada area penyimpangan dalam hidupku. Kita perlu menolong satu sama lain sebelum kita semua melenceng menuju kehancuran. Mungkin kita bisa bertahan, tetapi kita juga perlu mempedulikan anak-anak kita. Jika kita dapat berkumpul dan jujur kepada diri sendiri dan satu sama lain tentang apa yang jelas diajarkan Kitab Suci, maka kita akan lebih berhati-hati. Jika kita dapat mempelajari Firman Allah bersama, dengan hati dan pikiran yang terbuka, aku percaya kita dapat menguatkan apa yang masih tersisa. Aku percaya jika kita sujud di hadapan Allah, Dia akan menyembuhkan gereja-gereja kita. Semoga Allah memberkati kita semua dalam berjalan yang lebih dalam dengan Dia.

This hymn is universally thought to be one of the greatest hymns ever authored by a woman. It can be found in nearly every hymnal or book of hymns published today. This hymn writer was a woman of great ambition and enjoyment; a person full of life, vivacious, beautiful, talented, and a person who’s “exalted character always made a deep impression upon all who knew her”. Although she had a full and productive life, it was short, hastened on by her delicate and frail constitution. This hymn story has touched many lives in times of distress and hardship, including death. It has been used of God to draw the hearts of men from their present distresses, heavenward, to the immortal realities beyond this life.

Sarah Flower Adam was born at Harlow, England on February 22, 1805, to Benjamin and Eliza Flower. When she was five years old, her mother died of consumption, known today as tuberculosis. Sarah and her older sister Eliza also inherited the same physical weakness. Speaking of the hymn writer I quote from 101 Hymn Stories: “She was also widely known for her many literary accomplishments, though her delicate health was always a handicap for her many ambitions.”

In the year 1834, at the age of 29, Sarah married a prominent inventor and civil engineer, John Brydges. This distinguished couple made their home in London, England for the duration of their marriage, until the hymn writer’s death fourteen years later in 1848, at the early age of 43.

Sarah and her older sister Eliza made an outstanding team in the realm of music—writing and composing new songs. The elder sister being an accomplished musician, and the younger the hymn writer. One day their pastor, the Rev. William Johnson Fox, asked these two exceptional sisters if they would help him with the compilation for a new hymnal for his congregation. They committed to the project, and soon were busily occupied in helping him complete the song book. “Together, they contributed thirteen texts and sixty-two new tunes.”

One day as the two sisters were pressing into the task at hand, the pastor remarked that he wished he could have a hymn written to conclude a sermon he was preparing to preach on the account of Jacob and Esau. Eliza interrupted enthusiastically, “Sarah, now there’s an excellent idea for a new hymn for our hymnal. Why don’t you write your own hymn about Jacob’s dream?”

“Splendid!” replied the pastor. Later that day, after spending much time studying the Genesis account, absorbing the atmosphere, and feeling the dramatic movement of this Old Testament narrative, Sarah began to write. Soon she had versified the complete Biblical story into these five stanzas of the immortal hymn still in use today.

Nearer, my God, to Thee,
Nearer to Thee!
E’en though it be a cross
That raiseth me;
Still all my song would be,
Nearer, my God, to Thee,
Nearer to Thee!

Though like the wanderer,
The sun gone down,
Darkness be over me,
My rest a stone;
Yet in my dreams I’d be
Nearer, my God, to Thee,
Nearer to Thee!

There let the way appear,
Steps unto heaven:
All that Thou send’st to me
In mercy given;
Angels to beckon me
Nearer, my God, to Thee,
Nearer to Thee!

Then, with my waking thoughts
Bright with Thy praise,
Out of my stony griefs
Bethel I’ll raise;
So by my woes to be
Nearer, my God, to Thee,
Nearer to Thee!

Or if on joyful wing
Cleaving the sky,
Sun, moon, and stars forgot,
Upwards I fly,
Still all my song shall be,
Nearer, my God, to Thee,
Nearer to Thee!

This great hymn was written in 1840 and published the next year in the hymn book Hymns and Anthems prepared by Rev. Fox, the hymn writer’s pastor. The hymn’s original tune was a composition of Eliza, Sarah’s older sister. In 1844, Rev. James Freeman Clarke introduced the hymn in America, but it did not become well known for another 12 years. At that point the hymn was wedded with the present-day tune “Bethany” composed especially for the text by Lowell Mason, who is sometimes referred to as the father of American church and school music. Other hymns by Mason include “From Greenland’s Icy Mountains”, “When I Survey the Wondrous Cross”, “A Charge to Keep I Have”, “Joy to the World”, “My Faith Looks Up to Thee”, and “O Day of Rest and Gladness”.

Many very interesting accounts have been recorded in conjunction with the use of this hymn, and its effect on those who sang it or heard it sung. In the Boston Peace Jubilee of 1872, which commemorated the end of the civil war, this hymn, “Nearer, My God to Thee”, was sung by 50,000 voices. In 1871, three renowned theologians, Professors Hitchcock, Smith, and Park, were traveling in Palestine, when they heard the faint strains of “Bethany” reach their ears. Regarding this incident, I quote from A Treasury of Hymn Stories, “Drawing near, to their amazement, they saw fifty Syrian students standing under some trees in a circle, and singing in Arabic ‘Nearer, my God, to Thee,’ Professor Hitchcock, speaking afterward of the event, said that the singing of that Christian hymn by those Syrian youths moved him to tears, and affected him more than any singing he had ever heard before”.

During the Johnstown City Flood of May 31, 1889 (a tragic disaster that killed over 2,000 people), an unfortunate railroad train rushed into the swirling flood waters. A young woman, prepared to be a missionary, and on her way to the far east, became one of those trapped in a railroad car which was turned up on end. Beyond the hope of rescue, she spoke calmly to the awe-struck crowd as they gazed helplessly at the unfolding tragedy as the car sank beneath the muddy waters. She ended up with prayer and by singing “Nearer, my God, to Thee,” in which she was joined by the grieving and sympathizing throng. As she sang, she passed away, coming indeed nearer to her God whom she loved and desired to serve.

Last, but not least, in the wee hours of April 15th, 1912, the story of the sinking of the proud and ill-fated ship, the Titanic, brings this song to our memory yet again. Many survivors that witnessed this great tragedy have testified that the hymn “Nearer, my God to Thee” was the final song played before the cold waves of the Atlantic Ocean silenced her forever—as the band played, the great ship sank, plunging into the depths, sending over 1,500 souls into eternity.

In conclusion, it is incredible how much music and singing affect us. As we have seen from some of these accounts, from praise to peril, from thanksgiving to tragedy, from worship to the worst disasters that man may experience, God has given us this priceless gift in the timeless possession of the old-time hymns. May they never lose their luster in our lives or in the lives of our posterity, until that final day when time shall cease to exist.

Αυτός ο ύμνος θεωρείται παγίως ως ένας από τους σπουδαιότερους ύμνους που γράφτηκαν ποτέ από γυναίκα. Εμφανίζεται σχεδόν σε κάθε ύμνολογιο ή συλλογή ύμνων που εκδίδεται σήμερα. Η συντάκτρια του ύμνου ήταν γυναίκα μεγάλης φιλοδοξίας και ζωηρής χαράς· ένα πρόσωπο γεμάτο ζωή, ζωντάνια, ομορφιά, ταλέντο, και ένα άτομο του οποίου ο «υψηλός χαρακτήρας πάντα έκανε βαθιά εντύπωση σε όλους όσοι την γνώριζαν». Αν και είχε μια γεμάτη και παραγωγική ζωή, αυτή ήταν σύντομη, επισπευμένη από την εύθραυστη και λεπτή της υγεία. Η ιστορία αυτού του ύμνου έχει αγγίξει πολλές ζωές σε στιγμές στενοχώριας και δοκιμασίας, ακόμα και του θανάτου. Έχει χρησιμοποιηθεί από τον Θεό για να τραβήξει τις καρδιές των ανθρώπων από τις παρούσες θλίψεις, προς τα επουράνια, στις αθάνατες πραγματικότητες πέρα από αυτή τη ζωή.

Η Sarah Flower Adam γεννήθηκε στο Harlow της Αγγλίας στις 22 Φεβρουαρίου 1805, στον Benjamin και την Eliza Flower. Όταν ήταν πέντε ετών, η μητέρα της πέθανε από καχεξία, γνωστή σήμερα ως φυματίωση. Η Sarah και η μεγαλύτερη αδελφή της Eliza κληρονόμησαν επίσης την ίδια σωματική αδυναμία. Μιλώντας για τη συντάκτρια του ύμνου, παραθέτω από το 101 Hymn Stories: «Ήταν επίσης ευρέως γνωστή για τα πολλά λογοτεχνικά της επιτεύγματα, αν και η εύθραυστη υγεία της υπήρξε πάντα εμπόδιο για τις πολλές της φιλοδοξίες.»

Το 1834, σε ηλικία 29 ετών, η Sarah παντρεύτηκε έναν διακεκριμένο εφευρέτη και πολιτικό μηχανικό, τον John Brydges. Αυτό το επιφανούς κύρους ζευγάρι έζησε στο Λονδίνο της Αγγλίας για τη διάρκεια του γάμου τους, μέχρι τον θάνατο της συντάκτριας του ύμνου δεκατέσσερα χρόνια αργότερα, το 1848, σε μικρή ηλικία 43 ετών.

Η Sarah και η μεγαλύτερη αδελφή της Eliza αποτέλεσαν ένα εξαιρετικό δίδυμο στον τομέα της μουσικής—γράφοντας και μελοποιώντας νέα τραγούδια. Η μεγαλύτερη αδελφή ήταν μία πεπειραμένη μουσικός, και η νεότερη η στιχουργός των ύμνων. Μια μέρα ο πάστοράς τους, ο ιερωμένος William Johnson Fox, ζήτησε από αυτές τις δύο εξαιρετικές αδελφές αν θα τον βοηθούσαν στη σύνταξη ενός νέου ύμνολογίου για την ενορία του. Δέχτηκαν το εγχείρημα και σύντομα ασχολήθηκαν επιμελώς στη βοήθεια για την ολοκλήρωση του βιβλίου των τραγουδιών. «Μαζί, συνέβαλαν με δεκατρία κείμενα και εξήντα δύο νέες μελωδίες.»

Μια μέρα καθώς οι δύο αδελφές ασχολούνταν με το έργο, ο πάστορας παρατήρησε ότι θα ήθελε έναν ύμνο για να κλείσει ένα σκεπτόμενο κήρυγμα που ετοίμαζε πάνω στην ιστορία του Ιακώβ και του Ησαύ. Η Eliza διέκοψε ενθουσιωδώς, «Sarah, αυτό είναι εξαιρετική ιδέα για έναν νέο ύμνο στο ύμνολιό μας. Γιατί να μην γράψεις έναν δικό σου ύμνο για το όνειρο του Ιακώβ;»

«Υπέροχο!» απάντησε ο πάστορας. Αργότερα εκείνης της ημέρας, αφού πέρασε πολύ χρόνο μελετώντας την αφήγηση της Γένεσης, απορροφώντας την ατμόσφαιρα και νοιώθοντας την δραματική κίνηση αυτής της Παλαιάς Διαθήκης αφήγησης, η Sarah άρχισε να γράφει. Σύντομα είχε μετατρέψει ολόκληρη την Βιβλική ιστορία σε ποίηση σε αυτές τις πέντε στροφές του αθάνατου ύμνου που ακόμη χρησιμοποιείται σήμερα.

Κοντύτερα, Θεέ μου, σε Σένα,
Κοντύτερα σε Σένα!
Ακόμη κι αν είναι ένας σταυρός
Που με ανυψώνει;
Πάντα το τραγούδι μου θα είναι,
Κοντύτερα, Θεέ μου, σε Σένα,
Κοντύτερα σε Σένα!

Αν σαν τον περιπλανώμενο,
Ο ήλιος δυσεύγει,
Σκότος να πέσει πάνω μου,
Η ανάπαυσή μου πέτρα;
Κι όμως στα όνειρά μου θα είμαι
Κοντύτερα, Θεέ μου, σε Σένα,
Κοντύτερα σε Σένα!

Εκεί ας φανεί ο δρόμος,
Βήματα προς τον ουρανό:
Ό,τι μου στέλνεις εσύ
Με έλεος δίδεται;
Άγγελοι να με σκοτώσουν—όχι––να με κινήσουν— να με καλούν
Κοντύτερα, Θεέ μου, σε Σένα,
Κοντύτερα σε Σένα!

Τότε, με τις αφυπνισμένες σκέψεις μου
Λαμπρές με τον ύμνο Σου,
Από τις πετρώδεις λύπες μου
Θα ανυψώσω ένα Βηθέλ;
Έτσι διαμέσου των δεινών μου να είμαι
Κοντύτερα, Θεέ μου, σε Σένα,
Κοντύτερα σε Σένα!

Ή αν με χαρούμενο φτερούγισμα
Σχίζοντας τον ουρανό,
Ήλιος, φεγγάρι και αστέρια λησμονημένα,
Προς τα πάνω πετώ,
Πάντα το τραγούδι μου θα είναι,
Κοντύτερα, Θεέ μου, σε Σένα,
Κοντύτερα σε Σένα!

Αυτός ο σπουδαίος ύμνος γράφτηκε το 1840 και δημοσιεύτηκε έναν χρόνο αργότερα στο ύμνολογιο Hymns and Anthems που ετοίμασε ο ιερωμένος Fox, ο πάστορας της συντάκτριας. Η αρχική μελωδία του ύμνου ήταν σύνθεση της Eliza, της μεγαλύτερης αδελφής της Sarah. Το 1844, ο ιερωμένος James Freeman Clarke εισήγαγε τον ύμνο στην Αμερική, αλλά δεν έγινε ευρέως γνωστός για άλλα 12 χρόνια. Τότε ο ύμνος συνενώθηκε με την σημερινή μελωδία «Bethany» που συνέθεσε ειδικά για το κείμενο ο Lowell Mason, που μερικές φορές αποκαλείται πατέρας της αμερικανικής εκκλησιαστικής και σχολικής μουσικής. Άλλοι ύμνοι του Mason περιλαμβάνουν τα «From Greenland’s Icy Mountains», «When I Survey the Wondrous Cross», «A Charge to Keep I Have», «Joy to the World», «My Faith Looks Up to Thee», και «O Day of Rest and Gladness».

Έχουν καταγραφεί πολλές πολύ ενδιαφέρουσες μαρτυρίες συνδεδεμένες με τη χρήση αυτού του ύμνου, και την επίδρασή του σε όσους τον έψαλλαν ή άκουγαν να ψάλλεται. Στο Boston Peace Jubilee του 1872, που εόρταζε το τέλος του εμφυλίου πολέμου, αυτός ο ύμνος, «Nearer, My God to Thee», εψάλλη από 50.000 φωνές. Το 1871, τρεις διακεκριμένοι θεολόγοι, οι καθηγητές Hitchcock, Smith και Park, ταξίδευαν στην Παλαιστίνη, όταν άκουσαν τους αχνά ήχους της «Bethany» να φτάνουν στα αυτιά τους. Σχετικά με το επεισόδιο αυτό, παραθέτω από το A Treasury of Hymn Stories, «Πλησιάζοντας, προς κατάπληξή τους, είδαν πενήντα Σύρους φοιτητές να στέκονται κάτω από κάποια δέντρα σε κύκλο, και να ψάλλουν στα αραβικά ‘Nearer, my God, to Thee,’ Ο καθηγητής Hitchcock, μιλώντας αργότερα για το γεγονός, είπε ότι το άκουσμα αυτού του χριστιανικού ύμνου από εκείνους τους Σύρους νέους τον συγκίνησε σε δάκρυα, και τον επηρέασε περισσότερο από οποιοδήποτε άκουσμα που είχε ποτέ πριν.»

Κατά τη διάρκεια της πλημμύρας της πόλης Johnstown στις 31 Μαΐου 1889 (μια τραγωδία που σκότωσε πάνω από 2.000 ανθρώπους), ένα άτυχο τρένο εισήλθε στις αναταραγμένες πλημμυρισμένες υδάτινες μάζες. Μια νέα γυναίκα, προοριζόμενη να γίνει αποστολίδα και καθοδόν για την Άπω Ανατολή, έγινε μία από εκείνες που παγιδεύτηκαν σε ένα βαγόνι τρένου που αναποδογύρισε. Μπροστά στην απουσία ελπίδας διάσωσης, μίλησε ήρεμα στο έκπληκτο πλήθος καθώς αυτό στεκόταν αβοήθητο να κοιτάζει την εξελισσόμενη τραγωδία ενώ το βαγόνι βυθιζόταν στα λασπωμένα νερά. Τελείωσε με προσευχή και ψάλλοντας «Nearer, my God, to Thee,» στην οποία ενώθηκε το πενθών και συμπονετικό πλήθος. Καθώς τραγουδούσε, απεβίωσε, πράγματι πλησιέστερα προς τον Θεό της, που αγαπούσε και επιθυμούσε να υπηρετήσει.

Τέλος, αλλά όχι λιγότερο σημαντικό, στις πρώτες ώρες της 15ης Απριλίου 1912, η ιστορία της βύθισης του περήφανου και άτυχου πλοίου, του Titanic, φέρνει ξανά αυτό το τραγούδι στη μνήμη μας. Πολλοί επιζώντες που ήταν παρόντες σε αυτή τη μεγάλη τραγωδία έχουν καταθέσει ότι ο ύμνος «Nearer, my God to Thee» ήταν το τελευταίο τραγούδι που παίχθηκε πριν οι ψυχρές κυματώδεις του Ατλαντικού σιωπήσουν το πλοίο μια για πάντα — καθώς η ορχήστρα έπαιζε, το μεγάλο πλοίο βυθίστηκε, ρίχνοντας πάνω από 1.500 ψυχές στην αιωνιότητα.

Συμπερασματικά, είναι απίστευτο πόσο πολύ η μουσική και το ψαλμό επηρεάζουν εμάς. Όπως είδαμε από μερικές από αυτές τις μαρτυρίες, από τον έπαινο στη δοκιμασία, από την ευγνωμοσύνη στην τραγωδία, από τη λατρεία στις χειρότερες συμφορές που μπορεί να βιώσει ο άνθρωπος, ο Θεός μας χάρισε αυτό το ανεκτίμητο δώρο στην αειθαλή κληρονομιά των παλιών ύμνων. Είθε να μη χάσουν ποτέ τη λάμψη τους στη ζωή μας ή στη ζωή των απογόνων μας, μέχρι εκείνη την τελική ημέρα όταν ο χρόνος θα πάψει να υπάρχει.

Greetings of Christian love to one and all. In this issue of the magazine (Summer 2023)… The Church History article focuses on Bible prophecy pertaining to the end times and some various ways that over the years certain elements of the church got off track from the Biblical teaching as it pertained to their everyday life. In his article, Donny Brechbill, who together with his wife teaches multiple marriage seminars each year, endeavors to zone in on a challenging subject—some of the root problems that they see with women who are struggling in the church. Lee Rufener takes an unapologetic approach in his effort to share some expository teaching on practical ways to have a sanctified home. We have a new writer for the sisters this time who shares a burden on her heart—instilling God’s Word in the hearts of the next generation.

Plus, more interesting topics. Enjoy.

If you are edified or encouraged by any of the authors’ content, it would be a blessing for you to respond to us by mail or email. We pass this along to our writers for their benefit.

Recently, I was pondering the subject of change. As I have written before, we have gone through a fair bit of change as a family. During the last 1 to 2 years, we moved to another place of residence, I acquired a new job, and finally, praise the Lord, I have mostly recovered from most of the long-term effects of Covid. A special thanks to each one who has prayed for my health.

As I paused in quiet reminiscence, I was surprised by all the things that have changed in the 40-plus years that I can recall from memory. (Even though I am over 50 I really don’t remember much from the earliest years of my life.)

As a boy, I rode around in vehicles that had no seat belts and for sure, no airbags. When both of those “lifesaving” devices were first being introduced I well remember the many discussions whether they were truly lifesaving in their effect or whether the opposite was true. All vehicles used to be rear-wheel drive or four-wheel drive. How odd it seemed when the first front-wheel drive cars started to appear. Now we have hybrid vehicles with a push towards fully electric vehicles.

Forty-plus years ago, most farmers had gas-powered tractors with a carburetor or a diesel tractor with a manually powered injector pump. Today, most tractors are equipped with a computer and seemingly miles of wires and electronic this and electronic that. Back then, most farmers were able to maintain or repair their own equipment; now there is a need for diagnostic machines and specialized tools which cost a lot of money and take many hours to learn how to operate. This causes most farmers to rely on the expertise of specialized repairmen which also cost a lot of money.

Then there was Covid. That was a stressful time. Have you noticed what has changed during, after, or as a result of Covid? As I interact with others, routinely someone will say that this or that is different since Covid. Is it just me, or since Covid is the general public less friendly and more private with their interactions? Let’s check our own interactions to ensure that we are still being God’s “light” and “salt” to this dark world, and that we are not losing our “saltiness”. Also, there are help wanted signs everywhere. Why? It seems to me that Covid has encouraged what little work ethic was still flourishing in our society to diminish even further.

Then there is the issue of cell phones and E-bikes. What do these two disconnected products have in common? From my vantage point observing the Amish of Holmes County, these two items have done more to change a people and a culture in a more major way than almost anything else has in recent times.

Where does this all leave us? The Hebrew writer says that For the priesthood being changed, there is made of necessity a change also of the law –Hebrews 7:12. So, we see that God changed things as He saw fit, thus, if we need to change to become more Biblical, then we should. But the Apostle Paul says That we [should] henceforth be no more children, tossed to and fro, and carried about with every wind of doctrine… –Ephesians 4:14.

And because iniquity shall abound, the love of many shall wax cold. But he that shall endure unto the end, the same shall be saved –Matthew 24:12-13. So, let us be vigilant in these end times as change happens more and more around us. May we be among those who shall endure until the end.

Salamu za upendo wa Kikristo kwa wote. Katika toleo hili la jarida (Msimu wa Majira ya Joto 2023)… Makala ya Historia ya Kanisa inaangazia unabii wa Biblia unaohusiana na nyakati za mwisho na njia mbalimbali ambazo kwa miaka mingi baadhi ya vipengele vya kanisa vilipoteza mwelekeo kutoka kwa mafundisho ya Kibeberi kama yalivyoathiri maisha yao ya kila siku. Katika makala yake, Donny Brechbill, ambaye yeye pamoja na mkewe hufundisha semina kadhaa za ndoa kila mwaka, anajitahidi kuelemea mada changamoto—baadhi ya mizizi ya matatizo wanayoiona kwa wanawake wanaokumbwa na shida ndani ya kanisa. Lee Rufener anachukua njia isiyokuwa ya udhuru katika jitihada zake za kushiriki mafundisho ya upokezi juu ya njia za vitendo za kuwa na nyumba iliyo takatifu. Tuna mwandishi mpya kwa ajili ya dada wakati huu ambaye anashiriki mzigo moyoni mwake—kuwekeza Neno la Mungu mioyoni mwa kizazi kijacho.

Zaidi ya hayo, mada nyingine za kuvutia. Furahia.

Kama umejengwa au kupewa moyo na maudhui ya waandishi wowote, itakuwa baraka kwako kutujibu kwa barua au barua pepe. Tunapitia majibu haya kwa waandishi wetu kwa maslahi yao.

Hivi karibuni, nilikuwa nikitafakari kuhusu suala la mabadiliko. Kama nilivyoandika hapo awali, tumepitia mabadiliko kadhaa kama familia. Katika mwaka mmoja hadi miwili iliyopita, tulihamia mahali pengine pa makazi, nilipata kazi mpya, na mwisho, sifa kwa Bwana, nimepona kwa kiasi kikubwa kutokana na athari nyingi za muda mrefu za Covid. Shukrani maalum kwa kila mmoja aliyekuwa akiniombea afya yangu.

Nilikamia katika kumbukumbu kimya, nikashangazwa na mambo yote yametofautiana ndani ya zaidi ya miaka 40 ninayoweza kukumbuka kwa kumbukumbu. (Ingawa niko zaidi ya umri wa miaka 50 sidhani mengi sana kutoka miaka ya mwanzo ya maisha yangu.)

Kama mvulana, nilikuwa nikienda katika magari ambayo hayakuwa na mikanda ya kiti na hakika, hayakuwa na mifumo ya hewa. Wakati vifaa hivyo vya “kuokoa maisha” vilipoanza kuanzishwa nilikumbuka vizuri majadiliano mengi kuhusu kama kwa kweli vilikuwa vinakuokoa maisha kwa athari yao au kama kinyume chake kilikuwa kweli. Magari yote zamani yalikuwa na mwendo wa magurudumu ya nyuma au magurudumu manne. Ilionekana ajabu pale magari ya mwendo wa mbele yalipoanza kuonekana. Sasa tuna magari mseto (hybridi) na mwelekeo wa magari ya umeme kabisa.

Zaidi ya miaka arobaini, wakulima wengi walikuwa na trekta za mafuta yenye karabara au trekta za dizeli zilizo na pampu ya sindano inayowekwa kwa mkono. Leo, trekta nyingi zimewekwa kompyuta na kamba nyingi za waya na vifaa vya elektroniki hivi na hivyo. Wakati huo, wakulima wengi waliweza kutengeneza au kurekebisha vifaa vyao wenyewe; sasa kuna haja ya mashine za uchunguzi na zana maalum ambazo zinagharimu pesa nyingi na zinachukua masaa mengi kujifunza jinsi ya kuzitumia. Hii imesababisha wakulima wengi kutegemea ujuzi wa mafundi maalum ambao pia wanagharimu pesa nyingi.

Kisha kulikuwepo na Covid. Ile ilikuwa nyakati za msongo. Je, umeona mambo yalivyobadilika wakati wa, baada ya, au kwa sababu ya Covid? Ninapowasiliana na wengine, mara kwa mara mtu atasema kwamba hiki au kile kimekuwa tofauti tangu Covid. Je, ni mimi tu, au tangu Covid umma kwa ujumla umefanya kuwa rafikichanga na kuwa binafsi zaidi katika mwingiliano wao? Tukague mwingiliano wetu wenyewe ili kuhakikisha kwamba bado tunakuwa “taa” na “chumvi” ya Mungu kwa ulimwengu huu wa giza, na kwamba hatupotezi “ule kiwango chetu cha chumvi.” Pia, kuna matangazo ya kazi kutafuta wafanyakazi kila mahali. Kwa nini? Kwangu inaonekana kwamba Covid imehimiza maadili ya kazi yaliyobaki madogo katika jamii yetu kupungua hata zaidi.

Kisha kuna suala la simu za mkononi na baiskeli za umeme (E-bikes). Je, bidhaa hizi mbili zisizohusiana zina sifa gani sawa? Kwa mtazamo wangu ninayeitazama jamii ya Waamishi wa Holmes County, vitu hivi viwili vimebadilisha watu na utamaduni kwa njia kubwa zaidi kuliko karibu chochote kingine katika nyakati za hivi karibuni.

Haya yote yatutuacha wapi? Mwandishi wa Waebrania anasema kwamba Kwa kuwa huduma ya makuhani imebadilika, lazima pia sheria izingiwe—Waebrania 7:12. Hivyo, tunaona kwamba Mungu alibadilisha mambo kama alivyofikiri, kwa hivyo, tukihitaji kubadilika ili kuwa zaidi Kibeberi, basi tunapaswa. Lakini Mtume Paulo anasema Kwa hiyo tusivumilie tena kuwa watoto, wakorofishwaji na wabebaji kwa upepo wote wa mafundisho…—Waefeso 4:14.

Na kwa kuwa uovu utaongezeka, upendo wa wengi utazima. Lakini yule atakayevumilia mpaka mwisho, huyo atakuwa ameokoka—Mathayo 24:12-13. Kwa hivyo, tuwe waangalifu katika nyakati hizi za mwisho wakati mabadiliko yanapotokea zaidi na zaidi karibu nasi. Mungu atutii miongoni mwa wale watakaovumilia hadi mwisho.

For the unbelieving husband is sanctified by the wife, and the unbelieving wife is sanctified by the husband: else were your children unclean; but now are they holy … For what knowest thou, O wife, whether thou shalt save thy husband? or how knowest thou, O man, whether thou shalt save thy wife? –1 Corinthians 7:14-16.

As we gaze across the thoroughfare of homes surrounding us, we grieve as we behold one Christian tragedy after another. Almost every Christian has some near kin who has experienced divorce, a rebellious child, or strained marital relationships. Perhaps we cry out to God as we wonder why it is so, for it is surely not His plan. Herein we behold the apostle Paul bringing out an amazing principle that is little understood and even less employed—a sanctified home. It is what every sincere believer wants and seeks, but few apprehend. Christianity is not a rubber stamp that automatically clones offspring after the same sort. Still the scripture must be true and there must indeed be a sanctifying effect that a true believer brings into a home. This is no guarantee that the unbelieving spouse or the children of the union will be saved, but when a believing husband or wife acts in accordance with the scripture and the Spirit of God, the effect they have on the home will allow God’s power to be evident and an avenue of grace is poured into the pathway of all who dwell therein.

Our impotency is not caused due to the lack of God’s power, but because our dim understanding is infested and infiltrated with the influences of this present world. Faith in God alone is inevitably a powerful force, while faith injected by human reasoning and impatience will hardly prove any more effective than Abraham and Hagar’s attempts to produce a holy and sanctified child.

What then sanctifies the home? Casual observation will notice that merely being a believer isn’t enough to accomplish it. To sanctify is to make pure and holy. It is a process of filtering and a separation from that which is impure to bring greater purity to the object being sanctified. The Pharisees understood the principle well. They spent many a rigorous hour paying heed to countless miniscule details to make their vessels holy. Still, they were critically unsuccessful.

Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye make clean the outside of the cup and of the platter, but within they are full of extortion and excess. Thou blind Pharisee, cleanse first that which is within the cup and platter, that the outside of them may be clean also –Matthew 23:25-26.

The Inside Sanctified by Faith and Prayer

What a foolish thing it would be for a man to wash only the outside of a cup, which is to be looked at, and to leave the inside dirty, which is to be used. Yet there are those who avoid only the scandalous sins—those that would spoil their reputation with men—but would still allow themselves pride and moral decay in their heart. It is this which renders them odious to the pure and holy God. Such it is when a man or woman seeks to purify their home by superficial cleansing. Pharisaic attempts to root out and remove the surface details and inconsistencies from the lives of their helpmate and children, in order to sanctify them, are generally fruitless.

However quick-sighted they are in other things; Christ calls them blind. In Christ’s estimation, those who are not acquainted with the wickedness of their own hearts—those who see not, and hate not, the secret sin that is lodged within—are strangers to sanctification. Self-ignorance is the most shameful and hurtful ignorance. The rule is, “Cleanse first that which is within, to get cleansed from the filthiness of the spirit.” Corrupt affections and inclinations, the secret lusts that lurk in the soul, unseen and unobserved, these must first be recognized, mortified, and subdued. If due care is taken concerning that, the outside will, by extension, become clean also. External motives and inducements may keep the outside clean, while the inside remains filthy; but if renewed sanctifying grace makes the inside clean, that will have a lasting and profound influence upon the outside, for the commanding principle is within. If the heart is well kept, all is well, …for out of it are the issues of life –Proverbs 4:23.

Likewise, ye wives, be in subjection to your own husbands; that, if any obey not the word, they also may without the word be won by the conversation of the wives; While they behold your chaste conversation coupled with fear. Whose adorning let it not be that outward adorning of plaiting the hair, and of wearing of gold, or of putting on of apparel; But let it be the hidden man of the heart, in that which is not corruptible, even the ornament of a meek and quiet spirit, which is in the sight of God of great price. For after this manner in the old time the holy women also, who trusted in God, adorned themselves, being in subjection unto their own husbands: Even as Sara obeyed Abraham, calling him lord: whose daughters ye are, as long as ye do well, and are not afraid with any amazement. Likewise, ye husbands, dwell with them according to knowledge, giving honour unto the wife, as unto the weaker vessel, and as being heirs together of the grace of life; that your prayers be not hindered –1 Peter 3:1-7.

Here Peter speaks of a wife winning her husband with the due benevolence mentioned in Corinthians. While she has no unconditional guarantee of sanctifying her husband, she certainly will meet with little success without it. Eunice was a Jewess, who, upon embracing faith in Christ, found herself in an unequal yoke with a Greek. We read that unfeigned faith was first wrought in her mother Lois, and that affected Eunice. This, in turn, had a sanctifying effect on young Timothy, who was then prepared for the work of the Lord. We have no record that his father was added to the faith, but one can only imagine the initial turmoil within the breast of this young Jewess as she reverently honored her head and circumcised not her son but rather committed him to prayer. Here brings us to the other vital dimension of home sanctification. While she was not emboldened to teach her husband, she apparently had won his respect enough to allow her to teach her son in the home. This she diligently did… For it is sanctified by the word of God and prayer –1 Timothy 4:5.

And that from a child thou hast known the holy scriptures, which are able to make thee wise unto salvation through faith which is in Christ Jesus. All scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness –2 Timothy 3:15-16.

The Outside Sanctified by the Word

When the heart of the believer is dealt with first, the visible dimensions of the home fall into place in succession. Worldly influences have little appeal for the budding child of God. The Word of God must take its full place being administered to the children as well as the adults, for they are profitable for sanctification. A husband is to wash his wife and children (as well as himself) by administering the Word of God so that he may sanctify and cleanse his home.

Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the church, and gave himself for it; That he might sanctify and cleanse it with the washing of water by the word, That he might present it to himself a glorious church, not having spot, or wrinkle, or any such thing; but that it should be holy and without blemish –Ephesians 5:25-27.

When the Word of God is given full authority in the home, it becomes the governing principle around which the home operates. It must be allowed to filter out the media of the masses and the influences of all evil communications, which will corrupt good manners.

Blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly, nor standeth in the way of sinners, nor sitteth in the seat of the scornful –Psalm 1:1.

Individuals within the home may not always appreciate the direction received from it, but submit to it they must, and usually do so heartily. Most of us have received direction from our parents that we did not appreciate at the time but years later have come to grasp the blessedness of their leadership. Leadership that does not lead, is not expressing love, and will leave the home unsanctified and its members disconnected. Though it is rather uncomfortable and inconvenient to ask children to do without what others are partaking in, they are not sanctified by following their peers, but rather by the truth. For us as parents, there is no greater joy than to know that our children walk in truth. Equally so, there is no greater joy for them than to walk in it. Daily family devotions are a cohesive force within the home that is central and integral to home sanctification. We dare not apologize for the authority we give to the Word, nor slack from its use. It is an erroneous Gospel to believe that souls are stifled who are held to the mandates within it.

Here is Christ’s summation of His home.

I have manifested thy name unto the men which thou gavest me out of the world: thine they were, and thou gavest them me; and they have kept thy word. Now they have known that all things whatsoever thou hast given me are of thee. For I have given unto them the words which thou gavest me; and they have received them, and have known surely that I came out from thee, and they have believed that thou didst send me. I pray for them: I pray not for the world, but for them which thou hast given me; for they are thine. And all mine are thine, and thine are mine; and I am glorified in them. And now I am no more in the world, but these are in the world, and I come to thee. Holy Father, keep through thine own name those whom thou hast given me, that they may be one, as we are. While I was with them in the world, I kept them in thy name: those that thou gavest me I have kept, and none of them is lost, but the son of perdition; that the scripture might be fulfilled. And now come I to thee; and these things I speak in the world, that they might have my joy fulfilled in themselves. I have given them thy word; and the world hath hated them, because they are not of the world, even as I am not of the world. I pray not that thou shouldest take them out of the world, but that thou shouldest keep them from the evil. They are not of the world, even as I am not of the world. Sanctify them through thy truth: thy word is truth –John 17:6-17.

Christ, as the head of His home, employed no complicated means to the sanctification of His children. His life manifested a constant keeping Himself in the love of God through faith and prayer, and the administration of God’s Word to those about Him. At times they stumbled at it, wrestled inwardly, and misunderstood Him, but the keeping force rested not on the laurels of convincing words, adamant force, fun activities, nor prudent reasoning.

While a home must employ these resources from time to time, they of themselves do not carry the sanctifying power. For it is sanctified by the word of God and prayer –1 Timothy 4:5.
